denyListed.manualPath: chrome.scripting.executeScript with content.js, the same call the toolbar handler makes after its click; the toolbar icon click itself is not automatable in Puppeteer.

limitations: The native Chrome extension permission bubble (Allow/Deny) cannot be clicked by Puppeteer; tests pre-authorize through Chrome's own extensions site-access backend and then exercise chrome.permissions.request from a trusted click.

The toolbar icon click cannot be synthesized by Puppeteer. The manual path is verified by calling the same chrome.scripting.executeScript({files:['content.js']}) injection that the action handler performs.
Install-time host-prompt text and the All-sites warning text were checked in the settings/wizard DOM and manifest, not in Chrome's native install prompt.
T-31 was verified on local *.localhost fixtures with the built-in deny list extended by deny.localhost; real Gmail/Outlook/WhatsApp accounts were not opened.

defaultInstall.note: No optional origin is granted at install; the only host origin is the declared loopback Anki host. Chrome's install-time prompt text is not observable from automation.

permissionHarness.note: Exact origins were pre-authorized through Chrome's site-access backend, then chrome.permissions.request was invoked from a trusted click. The native Allow/Deny bubble was not automated.
